prompts.terrain: Use case: precise-object-edit. Image 1 is the EXACT empty-building terrain edit target. Image 2 is a development placement guide showing the exact FINAL building sprites at their actual map positions; use Image 2 ONLY to locate their FOOTINGS AND DOORS, never copy its functional buildings into the output. Edit Image 1 to paint a small amount of softly worn earth, paving or trampled grass directly UNDER AND AROUND THE ACTUAL FOOTINGS of the nineteen freestanding buildings shown in Image 2. Make those foundations and short entrance approaches feel naturally part of the landscape. These are modest ground stains and connected short paths, mostly concealed beneath the building bases later, NOT separate large round/oval/rectangular construction pads. Paint only immediately where the building's lower edge and service yard in Image 2 meet the ground, with soft irregular grass edges. Especially the Sawmill, Smithy, Workshop, Market and Builders' Yard must have their ground directly beneath the buildings as shown in Image 2; do not place a spare clearing down or to the side of any building. The royal Hall can have a restrained small courtyard immediately at its south entrance, not a large paving patch north of it. Keep the surrounding estate continuous olive grass, with NO isolated spare soil islands, piles of materials, fences or ghost building sites away from the provided actual bases. Every source pixel elsewhere retains the same landscape composition, city walls including their southern opening, roads, cottages, woods, mountains and farmland. Preserve exact 1448x1086 composition, viewpoint and framing; do not shift or rescale the scene. Fine umber ink, soft matte medieval atlas gouache, subdued olive/moss grass, ochre worn earth, warm pale stone and upper-left daylight exactly match Image 1. Output only the updated empty-building terrain as one opaque map illustration. NO functional buildings, Gatehouse, signs, stakes, scaffolding, text, labels, UI, guides or river. The completed buildings remain independent transparent sprites placed by the game; the ground you paint must look unobtrusive both before and after those buildings are added.
prompts.groundStudy:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Asset type: the opaque terrain plate for the Crownlands tiny city estate.
Input images: Image 1 is the exact terrain edit target. Image 2 is ONLY a placement guide: its rectangles identify future building reservations and must never appear in the finished illustration.
Primary request: make the ground beneath the nineteen freestanding building sites part of this hand-painted map, replacing the need for separate oval soil sprites. Within each guide reservation, clear obstructing shrubs and paint subtle, compact, irregular areas of worn earth or appropriate service-yard paving, joined naturally to the existing nearby dirt approach. Ground should blend organically into the olive turf and surrounding landscape; no repeated ellipses, rectangles, sharp patch borders or generic plot cards. The Great Hall can have a modest pale stone courtyard; farming and forestry sites have understated earth/turf; trade and crafts have worn compacted yards. Preserve green spaces.
Fixed site centers left/top %: Treasury39/33, GreatHall50/31, Barracks61/34, Alehouse40/46, RoyalStables60/48, GuildMaster40/54, Quarry29/18, Mine73/19, Forester17/33, Sawmill23/45, Smithy27/61, Workshop37/70, BuildersYard43/83, Windmill12/64, Farmstead18/79, Granary29/87, Storehouse69/63, WagonYard87/69, Market83/44.
Important invariants: same full 4:3 estate composition, camera angle and framing, same city-wall geometry and southern wall opening, same cottages outside the reservations, same roads, northern hills, western forest and southern fields. No river. Preserve the surrounding illustration closely. Do NOT add any functional landmark buildings, construction scaffolds, survey signs, or a Gatehouse in this pass: those remain independent structure layers. Do not add captions, numbers, guide lines, colored rectangles or UI.
Style: match Image1 exactly, thin brown ink outlines, matte painterly shading, olive grass, ochre worn earth, warm pale stone, gentle upper-left daylight. The clearings should feel painted by the same artist as the lanes and cottages, with varied unobtrusive edges. Return the complete estate terrain at its original composition, not a zoomed crop.
prompts.gateContext: Use case: precise-object-edit. Asset type: a close-up painting of the Crownlands southern city-wall junction. Image 1 is the exact edit target, a crop from the selected estate map, enlarged only as a guide. Paint a modest completed Gatehouse directly INTO this existing wall opening. Use the existing two square masonry wall-end towers as its feet: retain their precise ground locations, width, stone color, worn texture and angled connecting wall runs. Unite them with a short stone upper guard room and one open south-facing arch/raised portcullis centered on the existing dirt road. Small dark slate hip-roof caps may cover the two square guard towers, matching the other city wall towers. Tiny restrained burgundy pennants. No round towers, no conical fantasy spires. The Gatehouse should read as a part of this weathered enclosure, painted by the same artist, not as a crisp pasted icon. Keep it modest in height: the top is only about one existing wall-tower height above the original tower tops; keep both bases on the original ground line. The original outward-angled wall runs must flow naturally into the guard towers, with matching perspective, lighting, masonry thickness and crenellations. Keep the arch open so the actual pale dirt road is visible through it. Preserve the surrounding roads, grass, rocks, trees and cottages and EXACT framing of the input crop; do not zoom, recenter, change viewpoint, move the opening or redesign the walls. Improve painted detail at the higher source resolution while retaining the original shapes. Thin brown ink contours, soft matte painted shade, olive ground, warm pale grey stone, ochre road, upper-left daylight. Return an opaque contextual painting of this complete crop with the Gatehouse constructed in place. This in-map painting will then be extracted into a transparent building layer so placement must be exact. No labels, borders, interface or new ground platform.
prompts.backgroundRemovalStudy: Use case: precise-object-edit, background removal and building cutout. Image 1 is the completed Gatehouse painted into its actual Crownlands wall junction. Extract the central Gatehouse from this image as transparent PNG: ONLY the two square slate-roofed guard towers, both burgundy flags, and the connected stone guard wall with central arched gate between them. Preserve those exact pixels, colors, silhouette, scale and viewpoint as closely as possible. Delete the surrounding terrain, trees, cottage, rocks, roads, and long city wall runs that extend outside the two guard towers; those long wall runs already exist in the separate map plate. Remove the dirt and grass seen through the arch so that the entire opening below its masonry arch is transparent. Remove grass bushes in front of the masonry rather than leaving an opaque green patch. Retain delicate stone contact shading but no large ground island. CRITICAL: retain the entire input's 1448 by 1086 canvas and the Gatehouse's original positions within it (approximately x420 to1074, y541 to817). Do not center, enlarge, rescale, move, redesign or rotate the extracted building. Do not generate a new standalone gate design. The background must be truly transparent with clean alpha edges, including the opening; no checkerboard paint, white backdrop, frame or text. This cutout must be able to reconstruct its location perfectly when placed on top of the original scene.

detailTiles.nw: Use case: precise-object-edit. Asset: native high-detail nw terrain crop for Crownlands. Image 1 is the EXACT selected748x567 logical-map crop, which must be retained with identical framing and proportional placement. Output about1496x1134 pixels of genuinely drawn fine detail. Preserve every object and scene edge, the existing wall geometry and bare southern wall ends, roads and short dirt approaches, cottages, trees, rocks and fields. Retain the small subtle worn earth/paving areas precisely WHERE THEY CURRENTLY ARE; they sit beneath future building footings, so do not move, enlarge or emphasize them into isolated pads. Keep them empty, blending organically into grass. Add only small stone joints, slate lines, individual leaves, fine ruts and grass strokes in the same subdued medieval atlas painting style, warm umber ink, matte painted shading, olive/moss turf, ochre earth, warm pale stone and upper-left daylight. No new functional building, Gatehouse, supplies, fences, signs, stakes, scaffolds, people, animals, road changes, courtyard relocation, text, border or UI. No river. Do not zoom, extend, recenter, sharpen halos or blur the scene. This exact tile overlays its original coordinates on the full estate, so faithful registration with adjacent tiles and the building sprites is essential.
